note: Layers of protection is a safety engineering approach built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: multiple independent protective barriers are organized and deployed to manage process safety risk. The method serves safety-management by providing a structured framework for barrier management.

HAZOP is a structured safety analysis method built for the sake of safety-management: systematic examination of process deviations to identify hazards and safety implications. The study serves safety-management by producing findings that feed into risk controls and management decisions.

Safety data as a discipline (collecting, analyzing incident data, performance metrics) predates and fed into modern safety-automation systems. The which-came-first test confirms: systematic data collection about safety existed before automated systems could act on it.

A ladder is a specific kind of tool — an artifact that extends human capacity for reaching elevated positions. INSTANCE_OF per Law 9: a competent speaker calls a ladder 'a tool' (broad sense: artifact extending human capacity). The ladder is a concrete instance of the general category.

A safety-incident-report is produced/designed for the sake of hazard-assessment. Its purpose is to document incident details so hazards can be identified, evaluated, and mitigated. SERVES per Law 8d: the servant (report) points at the master (hazard-assessment). Removing the report format would not stop hazard-assessment from operating, but the report exists specifically to further it.

Safety-metrics are produced and maintained for the sake of hazard-assessment. They provide the quantified data that hazard-assessment operations need to evaluate risk levels and identify trends. SERVES per Law 8d: the servant (safety-metrics) points at the master (hazard-assessment).

An ontological category is a specific kind of classification scheme — a way of categorizing entities by their mode of existence or fundamental nature (e.g., substance, property, relation). A competent speaker would call an ontological category 'a classification' of being. Nearest kind is classification.

A status quo is a specific kind of concept — the idea of the existing state of affairs. It is a human-made construct used to refer to current arrangements. A competent speaker would describe it as a concept about the prevailing order.

A safety maturity model is designed and maintained for the sake of safety management. It provides the framework that safety managers use to assess, benchmark, and guide improvement of their safety programs. SERVES per Law 8d: the servant (maturity model) points at the master (safety management).

A safety incident report is produced for the sake of safety learning. Its purpose is to capture lessons from incidents so the organization can learn and improve. SERVES per Law 8d: the servant (incident report) points at the master (safety learning). This follows the same pattern as my accepted safety-automation → safety-management and safety-data → safety-analysis edges.

Safety education is built and maintained for the sake of safety-maturity-model: education builds the competencies and organizational knowledge that maturity models measure, benchmark, and seek to improve. The servant (education) points at the master (maturity model). SERVES per Law 8d.

Safety education is maintained for the sake of safety-dashboard: dashboards visualize education outcomes (training completion, competency levels, certification rates) so managers can monitor and improve educational effectiveness. SERVES per Law 8d: the servant (education) points at the master (dashboard).

A safety signoff is a specific kind of audit: both are formal verification processes where designated authorities examine evidence and render a judgment on compliance. The signoff specializes audit for safety-critical certification contexts.

Safety education is maintained for the sake of safety-management: it equips personnel with the knowledge and competencies that safety managers need to operate effective safety programs. Direction correct: servant (education) → master (management).

Safety signoff is maintained for the sake of safety-management: it provides the formal verification step that safety managers need to confirm controls are working. Direction: servant (signoff) → master (management), per Law 8d.

Safety data is collected and reported for the sake of safety-governance: governance bodies need accurate data to oversee safety performance and make policy decisions. Direction: servant (safety-data) → master (safety-governance).

A safety control is designed and deployed specifically for the sake of hazard mitigation. Its entire purpose — to eliminate, reduce, or mitigate a hazard — exists to further the operation of hazard-mitigation practice. For-whose-sake test: safety-control points AT hazard-mitigation as master.

Safety controls are deployed for the sake of achieving safety targets — their designed purpose is to further the operation of identifying, defining, and managing safety objectives. Per Law 8d, SERVES captures this teleological relation: servant (safety-control) points at master (safety-target).

Tested: causal-reasoning is the nearest kind. Cause-and-effect is a specific pattern of causal reasoning — identifying why things happen. A competent speaker would call it 'a form of causal reasoning.' Direction: specific→general per Law 9.

Safety-learning feeds safety-governance: governance depends on learning outputs (incident analysis, lessons-learned, training outcomes) to set policy, update procedures, and allocate resources. Learning is maintained for the sake of enabling effective governance.

Safety-monitoring provides continuous data, sensor readings, and observation records that hazard-assessment relies on to identify changes in risk profile. Its designed purpose is to supply the evidence base for assessment. SERVES direction: servant (monitoring)→master (assessment).

Safety-traceability links safety-relevant information (decisions, test results, incidents, design changes) across the lifecycle, enabling hazard-assessment to build on prior analysis and maintain continuity. Its designed purpose is to serve assessment's need for coherent records. SERVES direction: servant (traceability)→master (assessment).

Safety-assurance is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it provides the systematic checks, audits, and verification that safety-management needs to function. The designed purpose of assurance is to further management's operation per Law 8d.

Safety-knowledge-base is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it provides the structured information infrastructure — procedures, incident data, lessons learned — that managers need to plan, allocate, and direct safety activities. The designed purpose is to serve management with searchable, versioned safety knowledge.
Safety-audit is a specific method of safety-assurance. An audit is a systematic, independent examination — one concrete instance of the broader assurance concept. Specific→general per Law 9.

Safety-monitoring is designed and maintained for the sake of safety-incident: it continuously observes systems to detect incidents as they occur. The monitoring infrastructure exists to serve incident detection, response, and management. Servant→master per Law 8d.

Safety-simulation reproduces operational, fault, or emergency conditions to test responses. It is designed and maintained for the sake of safety-incident preparedness: building organizational readiness so real incidents are detected and handled effectively. Per Law 8d, servant (simulation) points at master (incident management).

Testing is a specific kind of assurance practice — the concrete verification activity within the broader assurance domain. Which-came-first: assurance as a concept predates formalized testing; testing is a specialized form of verifying safety measures.

Testing is designed and maintained for the sake of management oversight. The purpose of safety testing is to produce evidence for managerial decision-making about risk posture. Law 8d: servant (testing) points at master (management).

Safety-testing SERVES safety-readiness: testing exists to verify and confirm that personnel, procedures, and systems are prepared for safety functions. The designed purpose of testing is to produce readiness assurance, not to test for its own sake. Per Law 8d: the servant (testing) points at the master (readiness).

Safety-testing SERVES safety-resilience: testing safety-critical systems reveals weaknesses before failures occur, directly strengthening the organization's capacity to absorb and recover from safety events. The designed purpose of testing is to build resilient safety systems.

Safety-education SERVES safety-readiness: education builds the knowledge and skills that personnel need to be prepared for safety functions. The designed purpose of safety education is to produce competent, ready personnel.

safety-audit SERVES safety-compliance: audits are designed and maintained to verify that organizational processes, systems, and behaviors conform to safety requirements. The purpose of auditing is to produce compliance evidence — servant (audit) points to master (compliance). Law 8d satisfied.

A safety assessment is a specific kind of safety review: both are systematic evaluation activities, but assessment specifically measures the current state against criteria. A competent speaker would call an assessment a type of review.

Safety assessment serves safety management: assessments produce the data, metrics, and evaluations that management uses to make decisions, allocate resources, and control organizational safety performance. The designed purpose is to feed the management function.

Safety simulation serves safety assessment: simulations model scenarios to evaluate system behavior under stress, providing assessment data through what-if analysis. The designed purpose of simulation is to enable assessment of safety-critical situations without real-world risk.

Safety-monitoring serves safety-readiness: monitoring provides continuous data on system and personnel state, which is used to assess and maintain readiness levels. The designed purpose of monitoring is to produce the real-time information that readiness management needs.

Safety-testing serves safety-compliance: testing verifies that safety-critical systems meet established compliance requirements. The designed purpose of safety-testing is to produce evidence of compliance with safety standards and regulations.

Safety-drill serves safety-resilience: drills are designed exercises that build an organization's capacity to absorb, adapt to, and recover from safety events. The designed purpose of drills is to strengthen resilience through practiced response — the drill exists for the sake of resilience.

Safety planning is maintained for the sake of safety management: it produces the documented frameworks, objectives, and resource allocations that management uses to organize, direct, and coordinate all safety activities. Remove planning and management loses its structured basis for safety decision-making. The designed purpose of planning is to enable management's safety oversight.

safety-maturity SERVES safety-management: maturity models exist for the sake of management — they provide the assessment framework that management uses to track progress, prioritize investment, and drive continuous improvement in safety practices.

A safety-lapse is a specific kind of safety-incident: it describes a breach or failure in safety controls where risk exposure increases. The sense is clear — a lapse is an actual incident (not a near-miss) where safety controls failed. Direction: specific (lapse) → general (incident).

Safety-recovery is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: incident recovery plans are a core component of any safety management system, recovery teams report through safety management channels, and the success criteria of recovery (restored function, reduced risk) serve the overall safety management objective. Servant→master direction confirmed.

A bubble chart is a specific kind of pie chart variant: it shows parts of a whole as proportional bubbles radiating from a center, directly extending the pie-chart concept of area-proportional parts-to-whole representation.

A safety-signal is a specific kind of signal: one whose purpose is to communicate safety-relevant information (hazard presence, required action, system status) to observers. A competent speaker calls a safety signal a signal. This is the nearest kind — signal is the general category, safety-signal is a domain-specific instance.

Safety integration is the practice of embedding safety considerations into every phase of organizational operations — design, procurement, production, maintenance, decommissioning. Its entire purpose is to make safety-management operational rather than retrospective. For the sake of safety-management, safety-integration is the mechanism that ensures safety is not siloed but woven through all processes.

A conceptual framework for identifying, classifying, and managing risks serves safety-management by providing the risk taxonomy and assessment apparatus that management operations depend on. Purpose: risk framework exists to supply management with risk intelligence.

Safety-signaling communicates hazard presence, system status, and required action to observers. Its designed purpose is to serve safety-management by providing real-time situational awareness that management operations require.
Safety signs are physical signal devices built for the sake of safety-management: they communicate hazards, status, and required actions to enable management decisions and keep operations safe.

Safety integrity levels are classification metrics built for the sake of safety-assessment: they quantify the reliability requirements of safety functions, providing the numerical basis for assessing risk reduction needs.

Inherent safety is a design philosophy built for the sake of safety-management: it eliminates hazards at the source rather than controlling them, providing management with the most effective risk reduction strategy.
Safety-monitoring provides continuous data and anomaly detection that safety-testing depends on for targeted verification. Monitoring serves testing by identifying when and where tests are needed.

A safety risk is a specific kind of risk: the combination of likelihood and severity of harm to people, property, or the environment. A competent speaker calls it 'a risk' — it is risk scoped to the safety domain.

Safety-risk is identified, assessed, and managed for the sake of safety-integration. Safety-integration is the process of embedding safety considerations into every phase of system development; safety-risk is the domain whose analysis feeds that integration. The servant (safety-risk) points at the master (safety-integration).

Emergency-shutdown is built for the sake of safety-management: it is the emergency intervention procedure that safety management systems design and maintain. The servant (shutdown) points at the master (management).

What-if-analysis is maintained for the sake of safety-management: it systematically explores hypothetical failure scenarios to inform safety decisions and risk controls. The servant (analysis technique) points at the master (management).

Human-reliability is maintained for the sake of safety-management: it measures and models human error rates to inform safety decisions, training, and system design. The servant (reliability metric) points at the master (management).

Bubble chart is a specific kind of scatter plot: it displays data points as bubbles on x-y axes where a third dimension controls bubble size. A competent speaker would call a bubble chart 'a scatter plot.' Scatter plot is older (0.31 vs 0.35 epoch) and is the nearest kind.

Safety-investigation is a process maintained for the sake of safety-management: it systematically examines incidents and near-misses to generate findings that feed back into safety management systems. The servant (investigation) points at the master (management).

Safety-architecture is a structured framework maintained for the sake of safety-management: it organizes controls, governance, and compliance requirements into a design that safety managers use to allocate responsibilities, track verification, and ensure objectives propagate across system layers. The servant (architecture) points at the master (management).

safety-reporting is maintained for the sake of safety-investigation: reporting systems are designed to capture incident data so investigations can begin. Per Law 8d, the servant (reporting) points at the master (investigation). Reporting exists as a mechanism to enable systematic investigation.

safety-reporting is a specific kind of communication: structured organizational communication about safety matters. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call safety-reporting 'a communication' — it is a domain-specific form of communication focused on hazard and incident information exchange.

Management of change procedures are maintained for the sake of safety management: they ensure that organizational or system changes do not introduce uncontrolled safety risks. The MoC process serves as a control mechanism within the broader safety management system.

Permit to work systems are maintained for the sake of safety management: they authorize and control hazardous work activities to prevent accidents. The permit process serves as a procedural control within the safety management system.

Safety-reporting feeds incident and near-miss data into safety-architecture's feedback loops, enabling the framework to evolve controls and governance based on real-world evidence. Designed for the sake of safety-architecture's ongoing operation.

An ontological category is a classification concept designed for the sake of taxonomy — it provides the building blocks for systematic classification. The servant (ontological category) points at the master (taxonomy). Direction: servant→master.

Risk-treatment comprises the controls and measures selected to modify organizational risk — it is designed for the sake of safety-management, which selects, implements, and oversees these treatments. Remove risk-treatment and safety-management loses its primary lever.

Personal-protective-equipment (PPE) comprises gear worn to minimize exposure to hazards — it is designed and deployed for the sake of safety-management, which specifies, issues, and enforces PPE use. Remove PPE and safety-management loses a critical layer of its defense-in-depth.

The safety lifecycle is designed for the sake of safety management: it structures and sequences all safety-relevant activities so that safety management can systematically address hazards across the full system existence.

Near-miss reporting systems are designed and maintained for the sake of safety management: they provide early-warning data that enables management to identify trends, intervene proactively, and improve the safety culture.

Toolbox talks are safety briefings designed for the sake of safety management: they disseminate safety information, reinforce procedures, and build awareness as a sustained practice of organizational safety communication.

A violin plot is a specific kind of plot that displays distribution using a kernel density estimate. It extends the box plot with a rotated density shape. Pinning sense: statistical data visualization plot. The specific points at the general — a violin plot IS a plot.

A safety lifecycle is a specific kind of process — a structured sequence of safety-relevant activities from concept through disposal. Law 9: specific→general. The safety lifecycle follows a defined process framework (e.g. IEC 61508). A competent speaker would call a safety lifecycle 'a process'.

A radar chart is a specific kind of plot that displays multivariate data on a 2D chart with three or more quantitative variables represented on axes starting from the same point. Law 9: specific→general. A competent speaker would call a radar chart 'a plot'.
Toolbox-talk is a method of brief, focused safety communication designed to reinforce and align with established safety standards in the field. Its purpose is to make standards actionable.
Risk-treatment (selecting and implementing controls to modify risk) serves safety-critical-systems by ensuring their risk controls are properly applied to maintain safety integrity.

A scatter plot matrix is a specific kind of chart: a grid/array of scatter plots showing pairwise relationships across multiple variables. Nearest kind is chart (both epoch 0.31, chart is more foundational). Sense: scatter plot matrix as a multi-variable chart type.

Safety planning is the systematic process of defining, documenting, and organizing safety objectives and targets. Its designed purpose is to establish and achieve safety goals. Per Law 8d: the servant (safety-planning) points at the master (safety-goals). X is maintained for the sake of Y.

Safety assessment evaluates current safety performance against defined targets and identifies gaps. Its purpose is to inform and advance safety goals — it serves the goal-setting and goal-tracking process. Per Law 8d, servant→master.

Safety monitoring tracks ongoing safety performance metrics and KPIs against established targets. Its purpose is to measure progress toward and alert on deviations from safety goals. Per Law 8d SERVES: servant (monitoring)→master (goals).

safety-performance serves safety-goals: measuring and tracking safety achievement provides the feedback loop needed to assess whether safety goals are being met. Its designed purpose is to inform goal achievement — servant (performance measurement) points at master (goals), per Law 8d.

safety-instruction serves safety-management: teaching safety procedures and protocols is one of the key mechanisms through which safety management operates. Instruction exists to further the operation of the broader management system — servant (instruction) points at master (management), per Law 8d.
safety-performance measures and quantifies safety outcomes — it is a specific application/kind of measurement applied to the safety domain.

safety-culture is built and sustained for the sake of safety-management: it shapes organizational behavior, priorities, and daily decisions toward safety. Per Law 8d, the servant (culture) points at the master (management) — culture exists to make safety management effective.

safety-standards are established to guide and structure safety-management practice. Per Law 8d, standards serve management by providing the normative framework that management applies — the designed purpose is to further management's operation.

Hazard-reporting is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. It provides the upward flow of hazard data that enables management to identify, assess, and treat risks. Per Law 8d, the servant (hazard-reporting) points at the master (safety-management).

Safety-observation-report is produced for the sake of safety-management. It feeds frontline behavioral and procedural observations into the management system, enabling data-driven decisions. Per Law 8d, the servant (safety-observation-report) points at the master (safety-management).
dot plot is a specific kind of chart that uses dots to represent data values on an axis.
safety-briefing is a specific kind of briefing focused on conveying safety-related information and procedures. A safety-briefing IS a briefing.

Safety-briefing is designed and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it conveys critical safety information and procedures to ensure the safety management system operates effectively. The purpose is by design — briefings are built as a management tool. Servant→master direction: safety-briefing points at safety-management.

Safety-accountability is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it assigns responsibility, tracks compliance, and ensures that safety policies and procedures are actually followed. The purpose is by design — accountability mechanisms exist to make safety management effective, not to exist for their own sake. Direction correct: servant (safety-accountability) points at master (safety-management).
kpi (Key Performance Indicator) is a specific kind of metric used to evaluate success against objectives. A competent speaker would call a kpi 'a metric.' Nearest kind: metric.

Incident-reporting is a specific kind of process — a structured procedure for documenting and communicating incidents after they occur. Law 9 test passes: a competent speaker would call an incident-reporting 'a process.' Nearest kind: process.

Safety-policy is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it establishes the rules, standards, and expectations that safety-management then enforces and monitors. Purpose is by design — servant→master direction (Law 8d).

Incident-reporting is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it feeds documented incidents back into the management cycle so that management can learn, adapt, and prevent recurrence. Purpose is by design — servant→master (Law 8d).
A safety-inspection is a specific kind of audit focused on verifying compliance with safety requirements, standards, and procedures. Law 9.

Safety-reporting is built and maintained for the sake of detecting, documenting, and analyzing safety failures. Law 8d: the designed purpose is to further safety-failure awareness and prevention — the servant (reporting) points at the master (failure as the phenomenon being served).

Law 8d: safety-reporting is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. The designed purpose of safety-reporting is to feed information into safety-management decision-making: incident data, compliance metrics, trend analysis. The servant (reporting) points at the master (management). Removing safety-reporting would not stop safety-management from existing, but it would strip it of its primary feedback loop.

Law 9: a safety-failure is a specific case of risk — specifically, a risk that has materialized into harm or near-harm. A competent speaker would call a safety-failure 'a kind of risk event' or 'an realized risk'. Direction: specific→general. Test: the safety-failure definition carves it as the occurrence of harm from safety breakdown, which is a realized risk instance.

Safety-gates are decision points designed and maintained for the sake of safety-management. Per Law 8d, the servant (safety-gate) points at the master (safety-management): gates exist to institutionalize safety oversight within project lifecycles, feeding go/no-go decisions into the broader safety-management system. Remove gates and the systematic safety oversight of project stages stops operating.

Law 9: a near-miss is a specific case of safety-failure — specifically, a safety-failure where harm did not materialize but near-harm occurred. A competent speaker would call a near-miss 'a kind of safety event.' Direction: specific (near-miss) → general (safety-failure).

Law 7: hazard (a potential source of harm) conceptually predates risk (which adds probability/severity assessment). The risk concept builds on and derives from the older hazard concept. Historical check: hazard exists as a notion across ancient practices; formal risk quantification came later.

Law 8d: root-cause-analysis is built and maintained for the sake of safety-investigation. RCA is a method whose designed purpose is to further the operation of safety-investigation by identifying underlying causes. Servant (RCA) → master (safety-investigation).

hazard (a potential source of harm) is the older, broader concept. near-miss builds on hazard by adding the temporal qualifier — an event where the hazard was present but harm was averted. Which existed first? hazard as 'dangerous thing' predates near-miss as a technical safety term.

root-cause-analysis is a method built and maintained for the sake of investigating safety-failures. Its designed purpose is to identify underlying causes of failures. Law 8d: servant (RCA) points at master (safety-failure investigation/understanding).

Law 9: A toolbox-talk is a specific kind of safety exercise — a brief, informal safety discussion/exercise conducted by a work team before starting work. A toolbox-talk is a safety exercise that focuses on knowledge transfer and awareness.

Law 9: A safety-observation-report is a specific kind of incident-reporting — it documents observed unsafe conditions, near-misses, and safe behaviors. A competent speaker would call a safety observation report 'a kind of incident report' covering safety-relevant observations.

flow diagram IS a specific kind of diagram — a visual representation that maps process sequences. Law 9: the specific (flow diagram) points at the general (diagram). A competent speaker would call a flow diagram a type of diagram. The nearest-kind ladder: flow diagram INSTANCE_OF diagram.

A safety-program is an organization-wide framework built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. Per Law 8d, the servant (safety-program) points at the master (safety-management). The program exists to enable and structure safety management across the organization.

Safety-integrity provides quantified confidence measures that safety systems perform required functions — this metric serves safety-management by giving managers actionable data on system reliability and risk posture per Law 8d.

Safety-performance metrics and indicators serve safety-management by providing the data needed for oversight, course-correction, and accountability — the servant (measurement) points at the master (management) per Law 8d.

An emergency-procedure is a specific kind of procedure: a documented sequence of actions for handling emergencies. Per Law 9, a topic is a specific kind of its general category. A competent speaker would call an emergency procedure 'a procedure'.

A runbook is a specific kind of documentation: a set of operational procedures designed to handle common scenarios and problems. Per Law 9, a runbook is a kind of documentation artifact. A competent speaker would call a runbook 'documentation'.

safety-integrity is a specific kind of metric: a quantified measure of confidence in safety system performance. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call safety-integrity 'a metric' (specifically, a safety metric). Direction: specific → general. Nearest kind is 'metric' — no intermediate rung exists.

a safety-audit is a specific kind of audit: an examination focused on safety compliance, risk controls, and safety management systems. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls it 'a type of audit'. The nearest kind is audit.

Safety-reporting feeds data (incident data, observation logs, audit results) into safety-significance determinations. The reports exist to enable significance assessment — for-whose-sake: reporting→significance.

safety-significance is a specific kind of assessment — it assesses how significant or consequential a safety risk or event is. A competent speaker would call safety-significance 'an assessment.' It files against the nearest kind.

safety-reporting as a broad practice contains incident-reporting as a core sub-component. A safety-reporting system is literally composed of incident reports, observation reports, audit reports, and other report types — incident-reporting is a part inside the whole.

A trailing indicator is a specific kind of safety indicator — one that looks backward at actual harm events rather than forward at leading signals. A competent speaker calls a trailing indicator 'a safety indicator.' Nearest kind: safety-indicator already exists (ACCEPTED), so this files against the correct rung on the ladder.

Trailing indicators are designed and maintained for the sake of evaluating past safety performance. They quantify actual harm events, near-misses, and failures specifically to answer how well the safety system has performed. Law 8d: for-whose-sake test — reporting and measurement serve performance evaluation.

Safety-culture assessment is maintained for the sake of safety management — it evaluates the cultural foundations that enable or undermine safety practices. Law 8d: designed purpose is to inform management decisions about culture improvement. The servant (assessment) points at the master (management).

Leading indicators are maintained for the sake of safety management — they provide early warning of deteriorating conditions so management can act before incidents occur. Law 8d: designed purpose is proactive management intervention. The servant (indicator) points at the master (management).
A safety-climate survey is a specific kind of assessment — it measures attitudes, beliefs, and perceptions about safety. A competent speaker calls it an assessment of organizational safety climate.
Safety committees are established for the sake of safety management — they advise, coordinate, and drive safety initiatives. Law 8d: designed purpose is to further safety-management operation.

Hazard communication is designed to convey safety-relevant information about dangerous substances, conditions, and practices to those who may be exposed — its purpose is to enable safety management. Law 8d: servant→master.

safety-analysis is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. Its designed purpose is to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks so that safety-management can make informed decisions. Remove safety-analysis and safety-management loses its primary analytical tool — it still operates but is starved of the evidence it needs to function effectively.

risk assessment is a specific kind of assessment — a systematic evaluation of potential risks and their consequences. A competent speaker would say 'risk assessment is a type of assessment.' The nearest kind is assessment, which captures the evaluative method common to both.

which came first? safety-management as a practice and concept predates specific safety goals. Goals are artifacts derived from the broader management framework. Law 7: safety-management existed first and fed into the creation of safety goals.

emergency-plan is a specific kind of plan — one focused on preparing for and responding to emergencies. A competent speaker would say 'an emergency plan is a type of plan.' Law 9: specific→general to the nearest kind.

safety-metrics is a specific kind of metric — measurements specifically tracking safety performance, indicators, and outcomes. Law 9: a competent speaker would call safety-metrics 'a type of metric.' Nearest kind is metric.

safety-dashboard is a specific kind of dashboard — one that displays safety-relevant data, KPIs, and indicators in a unified view. Law 9: specific→general. A competent speaker calls it 'a type of dashboard.' Nearest kind is dashboard.

safety-criterion is a specific kind of criterion — one that sets safety-related standards and benchmarks. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a safety-criterion 'a type of criterion.' Nearest kind is criterion.

incident-reporting is a specific kind of safety-reporting — it reports safety-relevant incidents (near-misses, injuries, property damage). A competent speaker calls it 'a type of safety report.' Nearest kind: safety-reporting is more specific than general safety-management.
Test: which existed first? Standards (generic) predate safety-specific ones by centuries. The generic practice of standard-setting came first and fed into domain-specific safety standards.

Safety-standards are built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. They provide the formal requirements and guidelines that safety-management processes use to establish controls. The designed purpose of a safety-standard is to further safety-management's operation — you remove standards and safety-management loses its normative framework.

Safety-protocols are codified procedures designed to support safety-management operations. They specify required actions and prohibitions that safety-management enforces. Their purpose is to further safety-management's ability to prevent and manage risks — they serve the management function by being the actionable rules that management implements.

Safety-criteria are benchmarks specifying acceptable safety levels used directly by safety-management processes. Management relies on criteria to evaluate performance, set targets, and judge compliance. The designed purpose of safety-criteria is to serve safety-management's decision-making and control functions.
A safety-checklist is a specific kind of checklist instantiated for safety-critical verification tasks. Per Law 9: specific→general. A competent speaker would call a safety-checklist 'a checklist'.

A safety-checklist is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. It provides a verification tool that safety-management processes use to ensure procedures are completed. Servant→master per Law 8d.

A safety-leading-indicator is a specific kind of metric: it measures proactive activities and conditions that predict future safety performance, rather than tracking past failures. Nearest kind is metric. Law 9: specific→general.
A safety-criterion is a specific kind of metric: it specifies a quantifiable or qualitative benchmark for acceptable safety performance levels. Nearest kind is metric. Law 9: specific→general.

safety-participation is designed and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it provides the worker input that makes safety governance effective, legitimate, and grounded in frontline reality. The servant (participation) points at the master (management). Safety-management can operate without participation, but it is poorer for it — purpose, not necessity, is the relation.

safety-feedback is a specific kind of feedback — the sense pinned is organizational feedback about safety performance, not biological or electronic feedback. A competent speaker would call safety-feedback 'a feedback.' Nearest kind is feedback itself, not a more general category.
Safety-training is a specific kind of training focused on safety knowledge, procedures, and competencies. It is a domain-specific instance of the general training construct.

Safety-awareness is cultivated and maintained for the sake of safe operations — its designed purpose is to make hazard recognition automatic, furthering safety-management's operation. Per Law 8d: the servant (safety-awareness) points at the master (safety-management). Removing safety-awareness does not stop safety-management from operating (it still has training, procedures, monitoring), but it ceases to have its cognitive vigilance layer.

Incident-investigation is a specific kind of root-cause-analysis focused on analyzing accidents and near-misses after they occur. Root-cause-analysis is the general method; incident-investigation is its domain-specific application.

A safety-knowledge-base is a specific kind of knowledge-base dedicated to safety information, standards, procedures, and lessons learned. It is the general knowledge-base construct specialized for the safety domain.

coaching INSTANCE_OF training per Law 9: 'coaching is a specific kind of training' focused on individual development, performance improvement, and goal-setting rather than skill acquisition. Nearest kind is training. A competent speaker would call coaching 'a form of training.'

A safety briefing is a specific kind of safety communication — it is a structured, timed, often mandatory session designed to convey safety information to a defined audience. A competent speaker would call it 'a kind of safety communication' (Law 9). The nearest kind is safety-communication, as briefings are a delivery modality within the safety communication construct.

safety-leading-indicator is a specific kind of leading-indicator applied to the safety domain. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a safety-specific leading indicator 'a leading indicator.' Nearest kind is leading-indicator (not metric, since leading-indicator is already the immediate category).
A safety-baseline-metric is a specific kind of metric used as a baseline for safety assessment. Law 9: a competent speaker would call it a metric. Nearest kind is metric.

Transparency is built and maintained for the sake of accountability. Law 8d: the servant (transparency) points at the master (accountability). Without transparency, accountability cannot function — you can't hold parties responsible for actions no one can see.

A key-performance indicator is a specific kind of metric — a quantified measure for evaluating organizational success against strategic objectives. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a KPI 'a metric.' Files against nearest kind: metric.

A trailing indicator is a specific kind of metric — it is a quantified measurement (the most recent value in a time-ordered sequence) used to assess current state or trend. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a trailing indicator 'a metric.' Files against nearest kind 'metric'.

A safety-trailing-indicator is a specific kind of trailing-indicator — it is the most recent value in a time-ordered sequence of safety measurements, used to assess current safety state or short-term safety trend. Law 9: a competent speaker would call a safety-trailing-indicator 'a trailing-indicator.' Files against the nearest kind.

Safety-investment is deliberately built and sustained for the sake of safety-protection. The purpose of allocating resources toward safety (training, equipment, audits, culture programs) is to achieve and maintain protection. Law 8d: for whose sake? The servant (investment) points at the master (protection).

A safety-lapse (a momentary deviation from safety protocols or a slip in vigilance) is a specific kind of safety-failure. A safety-failure is any breakdown in the safety system; a lapse is one particular form of that breakdown — distinct from a safety-violation (deliberate) or safety-deficiency (structural). Law 9: specific→general.

A safety-threshold is established and maintained for the sake of safety-protection. Its designed purpose is to mark the boundary of acceptable risk so that protective measures can be calibrated and triggered. The threshold serves the protection function — it exists to make protection actionable.

A safety-threshold is a specific kind of metric: a defined standard for measurement that marks a boundary. A competent speaker would call a threshold 'a metric' — it provides the quantitative or qualitative standard against which safety status is measured. This pins the metric sense as a standard/boundary of measurement, not just any data point.

Pre-test: which came first? Investment predates safety-investment. Safety-investment is a specific kind of investment: allocation of resources toward a domain. A competent speaker calls it 'an investment in safety'. Nearest kind.

Pre-test: remove protocol — does safety-lapse stop OPERATING? Yes. A safety-lapse IS a deviation from a safety protocol; without the protocol there is no standard to deviate from, and the concept cannot function. This is present-tense operational dependency, not historical association.

Pre-test: incident-investigation is a specific kind of procedure — a structured process for examining incidents after they occur to determine causes and prevent recurrence. A competent speaker would say 'incident investigation is a procedure.' Nearest kind is procedure (not risk-assessment, which is the analytical activity, not the procedural framework).

Pre-test: safety-isolation is a specific kind of safety control — a method that isolates hazards or risks from people, systems, or other hazards. A competent speaker calls it 'a safety control.' Nearest kind is safety-control (not hazard-mitigation which is broader — isolation is a specific control technique).

Pre-test: Safety trailing indicators serve safety protection — their designed purpose is to further safety protection's operation by providing early signals about deteriorating safety conditions. For whose sake? The trailing indicator serves the protection it monitors. Safety-protection is the master; the indicator is the servant.

Pre-test: safety-baseline is a specific kind of safety-metric — a defined reference point against which safety conditions are measured. A competent speaker would call a safety baseline 'a safety metric.' Nearest kind is safety-metric, not the broader metric.

preventive-action is built for the sake of safety-management. Its designed purpose is to further safety-management's operation by identifying and eliminating root causes before they materialize. Servant (preventive-action) points at master (safety-management).

risk-control practices are built for the sake of safety-management. Their designed purpose is to further safety-management's operation by identifying, evaluating, and controlling risks. Servant (risk-control) points at master (safety-management).

safety-intervention is a specific kind of preventive-action — it is preventive action specialized to safety contexts. A safety intervention IS a preventive action (Law 9). Direction: specific (safety-intervention) → general (preventive-action).

preventive-action is a specific kind of risk-management practice — it identifies and eliminates root causes of potential nonconformities before they materialize. A competent speaker would call preventive-action 'a risk-management technique' (Law 9).
risk-control is a specific kind of risk-management practice — it identifies, evaluates, and controls risks. A competent speaker would call risk-control 'a risk-management technique' (Law 9).

safety-gate is a specific kind of safety-management mechanism — a formal decision point in a process or project lifecycle that must be cleared before proceeding to the next stage. It is a management checkpoint, making it a specific type of safety management practice.

safety-accountability is a specific kind of safety-management structure — the assignment and verification of responsibility for safety outcomes within an organization. It is a management mechanism for ensuring safety obligations are met.

Pre-test: poka-yoke is a specific kind of method — a mistake-proofing method built into a process. A competent speaker would call it a type of method (specifically, a quality/prevention method). Nearest kind: method exists.

Error-prevention is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. The servant points to the master: error-prevention serves the broader discipline of managing organizational safety. This is teleological, not constitutive — error-prevention is a key practice within safety management's domain.

Pre-test: safety-program is a specific kind of safety-management — a structured, organized approach to managing safety in an organization. A competent speaker would call it 'a type of safety management framework.' Nearest kind: safety-management.

Pre-test: safety-instruction is a specific kind of procedure — a structured instructional procedure for conveying safety knowledge and practices. A competent speaker would call it 'a type of procedure' (specifically, an instructional procedure). Nearest kind: procedure (already the target of incident-investigation INSTANCE_OF→procedure).

Pre-test: safety-recovery is a specific kind of procedure — a structured recovery procedure following safety incidents. A competent speaker would call it 'a type of procedure' (specifically, a recovery procedure). Nearest kind: procedure.

Status quo depends on norms: the concept of the current established state of affairs requires existing norms or conventions to give meaning to 'status.' Remove norms and the concept of status quo loses its referent — there is no 'status' without standards. This is an object-level dependency, not meta-level.

Safety-program (the structured organizational framework) contains safety-instruction (instructional procedures for conveying safety knowledge) as one of its component parts — a safety program's instructional/training component.

Safety-program (the structured organizational framework) contains safety-recovery (recovery procedures following safety incidents) as one of its component parts — the incident recovery component of the program.

Error-prevention evolved from risk-management: risk management (identifying and assessing risks) existed first and fed into the more focused discipline of error-prevention (designed specifically to stop human/organizational errors before they occur). Historical lineage.

Scrum is a specific kind of methodology — a system of methods for project management. A competent speaker would call scrum 'a project management methodology'. Files against nearest kind (methodology).

A safety-objective is a specific kind of safety-management construct — it defines the goal state that safety-management systems work to achieve. A competent speaker would call a safety-objective 'a safety-management goal/plan'.

A safety-maturity model is a specific kind of safety-management construct. It provides a structured framework (typically with defined levels/stages) to assess and advance an organization's safety-management system. A competent speaker would call a maturity model 'a safety-management framework/method.' FILES INSTANCE_OF to the nearest kind.

A safety-target is a specific kind of safety-management construct — it is a quantified goal or metric within a safety-management system (e.g., TRIR target, leading indicator thresholds). A competent speaker would call a safety-target 'a safety-management metric/goal.' Files INSTANCE_OF to the nearest kind.

A safety program contains safety objectives as constituent parts. The program is structured around specific objectives it seeks to achieve — removing the objectives would collapse the program's operational purpose.

Safety management as a system contains individual safety programs as structural parts. A safety program is a constituent element of a broader safety-management framework — removing the programs leaves the system without its operational mechanisms.

A safety-trainer IS a specific kind of safety-management construct — it is a structured mechanism (person, tool, or process) designed to train others in safety knowledge and practices. A competent speaker would call a safety-trainer 'a type of safety management resource'.

A safety moment is a short safety briefing or discussion delivered at the start of meetings. It serves safety management by keeping safety top of mind and reinforcing safety culture — its designed purpose is to further safety-management's operation, not to be a constituent part of it.

A safety trainer (person, tool, or process for training in safety) serves safety management by executing its educational function. Its designed purpose is to further safety-management's operation — training others so the broader management system achieves its aims.

Safety communication (the practice of conveying safety information) serves safety management. Its designed purpose is to further safety-management's operation by ensuring information flows to those who need it — communication is the nervous system of the management function.
A bottleneck IS a specific kind of constraint — namely, the constraint that limits system throughput. A competent speaker would call a bottleneck 'a constraint' (the throughput-limiting kind).

Competency programs are designed and maintained for the sake of safety-management: they ensure workers have the demonstrated ability to perform tasks safely. The designed purpose is to further safety-management's operation by providing a framework for assessing and maintaining safe performance capability.

Safety-competition IS a specific kind of safety-management — namely, using competitive incentives (contests, gamification, safety rankings) to motivate safer behavior and improve safety outcomes. A competent speaker would call safety-competition 'a safety-management approach'. Files against the nearest kind.
indicator IS a specific kind of sign — a marker or data point that conveys information about a condition or trend. A competent speaker calls an indicator a sign. INSTANCE_OF per Law 9.

A safety-KPI is a specific kind of safety-management instrument: a quantifiable measure designated critical for organizational safety success. Per Law 9, it IS a kind of safety management tool, not a part or dependency.

Safety-traceability is a specific kind of safety-management tool: the practice of tracking and documenting safety-related events, exposures, and outcomes for accountability and improvement. A competent speaker calls it a safety management technique. Per Law 9.

safety-kpi SERVES safety-management: a KPI is designed for the sake of safety management — its purpose is to provide decision-relevant signals to safety managers. Per Law 8d, serving Y is not needing Y; remove trade and logistics still moves armies.

A safety-significance is a specific kind of criterion — the weight or importance assigned to a safety factor when judging risk or priority. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls it 'a significance criterion' in context.

Per Law 9, a near-miss is a specific kind of indicator — an observable event that signals something noteworthy occurred. A competent speaker calls it 'a type of indicator' in safety contexts. Near-miss is a specific instance of the general concept of indicator.

Per Law 9, a near-miss is a specific kind of safety-symptom — an observable indicator that a safety failure or incident may be imminent. A near-miss is a concrete type of safety-symptom, which is the broader category of early warning signs in safety management.

A safety-protocol is a specific kind of procedure — a standardized set of safety steps that must be followed. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls it a 'safety procedure.' Direction: specific (protocol) → general (procedure).

Safety-feedback is a specific kind of safety-management construct — a structured mechanism for reporting, analyzing, and acting on safety-related information. Per Law 9, it is a kind of safety-management practice. Direction: specific → general.

Per Law 9, an early-warning is a specific kind of indicator — it signals that something is about to happen, indicating future risk or change before it occurs. The note pins the sense: early-warning as a predictive signal, which is a subtype of the general concept of indicator.

Per Law 9, a safety-symptom is a specific kind of indicator — it signals the presence of an unsafe condition or emerging risk. Symptoms are observable signs that indicate underlying states, making them a subtype of indicators.

Safety-goal is a specific kind of safety-management construct: a target set within a safety management system to direct safety improvement. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call a safety-goal a kind of safety-management practice. The note pins the sense as goal-setting within safety management.

Leading-indicator is a specific kind of indicator that signals future risk or performance trends, not past outcomes. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call a leading-indicator an indicator. Files against the nearest kind — indicator is the direct parent.

Safety-participation is a specific kind of safety-management practice: activities that engage workers in safety processes (committees, reporting, suggestions). Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call it a kind of safety-management approach. The note pins the sense as participatory safety practices.

Remove indicators and a safety-symptom ceases to function — a symptom IS an indicator of unsafe conditions. Without the indicator mechanism (signaling), the concept of a safety-symptom has no operational role. This is not about sayability (Law 2b) but about the actual working of X.

A safety-procedure IS a specific kind of procedure — a standardized sequence of steps. A competent speaker would call a safety-procedure 'a procedure' (specifically, a safety-related one). Files against the nearest kind (procedure, already ACCEPTED). Law 9 satisfied.
A safety-system CONTAINS safety-procedures as structural components — the documented steps and protocols are literal parts that make up the overall framework. Whole-part relation, Law 10 satisfied.

A safety-kpi IS a specific kind of safety-metric — it is a quantifiable measure of safety performance. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls a safety-kpi 'a safety-metric' (specifically, one designated as critical). Files against the nearest kind: safety-metric.

Safety competencies are developed, maintained, and assessed for the sake of safety management. Per Law 8d: safety management is the master, safety competencies serve it. The designed purpose of competency programs is to further safety management's operation.

Safety procedures are established and maintained for the sake of safety management. Per Law 8d: safety management is the master, procedures serve it. Their designed purpose is to further safety management's operation by standardizing safe performance.

Poka-yoke IS a specific kind of error-prevention technique — a mistake-proofing device or procedure designed to prevent errors before they occur. Law 9: a competent speaker calls poka-yoke 'an error-prevention' method. Files against the nearest kind.

Safety-procedures derive from safety-policies: policies existed first (epoch 0 vs 0.27) and fed into procedures. A procedure is a detailed step sequence mandated by a higher-level policy. Which-came-first test: policy predates and conceptually precedes the procedure.

Remove safety-culture and the safety-system stops OPERATING — not merely becoming sayable. A safety system's mechanisms (reporting, compliance, enforcement) require a culture that values safety to function. People must care about safety for the system's procedures to actually work. Object-level dependency, not meta-level.

safety-competency is a specific kind of competency — the domain-specific variant focused on safe work performance. Law 9: a competent speaker would call safety-competency 'a competency.' Nearest kind: competency.

hazard-identification is built and maintained for the sake of risk assessment. Law 8d: risk-assessment is the master, hazard-identification serves it. Hazard ID is the first step that feeds into the risk assessment process — by design.

A trailing-indicator IS a specific kind of indicator — a metric that reflects past safety performance after events have occurred. Like leading-indicators (which predict future risk), trailing-indicators are a subtype of indicator distinguished by temporal direction. Law 9: a competent speaker calls a trailing-indicator 'an indicator.'

safety-intervention IS a specific kind of safety-management — a deliberate organizational action designed to correct unsafe conditions or behaviors before harm occurs. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call it 'a safety management action.' Nearest kind: safety-management.

Test: remove safety-competency as a goal — does safety-training stop operating? No, it still trains. But safety-training is DESIGNED and maintained for the sake of building safety-competency. Per Law 8d: for-whose-sake? servant(safety-training)→master(safety-competency). Purpose by design, not incidental benefit.

safety-reporting IS a specific kind of safety-management. A competent speaker would call it a safety management practice — incident and near-miss reporting is a core operational function within the safety management system. Law 9: specific→general. (Corrects my earlier CONTAINS error; this is a kind-of relation, not whole-part.)

Safety-momentum needs safety-management to operate: the active force/direction of safety efforts requires management's structures, resources, and processes to be sustained. Without management scaffolding, momentum dissipates. Per Law 8 removal test: remove safety-management now, and safety-momentum has no channel to persist — it stops operating as organized momentum.

Per Law 8d: hazard-register is designed and maintained for the sake of risk-assessment. The register provides the structured hazard data that risk-assessment needs to evaluate risk levels and prioritize controls. Without the register, risk-assessment has no systematic input — it loses its data source.
safety-standards IS a specific kind of safety-management. A competent speaker would call safety standards a safety management mechanism — standardized rules and requirements for managing safety.
safety-inspection IS a specific kind of safety-management. Systematic examination of conditions/processes for compliance is a core safety management practice.

A hazard-register is a specific kind of register — a systematic record of identified hazards. A competent speaker would call a hazard register 'a type of register'. Nearest kind: register (a documented list), not inventory.

A safety-watch IS a specific kind of safety management — a systematic practice of monitoring conditions and behaviors to prevent incidents. A competent speaker would call safety watch a form of safety management. Nearest kind: safety-management.

Hazard-reporting IS a specific kind of safety-reporting — reporting that focuses specifically on identifying and documenting hazards. A competent speaker would call hazard reporting a type of safety reporting. Nearest kind: safety-reporting.

Per Law 8d: hazard-reporting is designed and maintained for the sake of hazard-register — the reporting practice feeds structured data into the register. The servant (hazard-reporting) points at the master (hazard-register).

safety-kpi SERVES safety-watch per Law 8d: the KPI metric is designed and maintained for the sake of safety-watch. KPI data feeds into the monitoring practice, enabling safety-watch to evaluate performance and detect issues.

Safety-watch IS a specific kind of practice — a systematic practice of monitoring conditions and behaviors. A competent speaker calls it 'a safety practice.' Nearest kind is practice, not indicator or management.

Safety-momentum SERVES safety-management per Law 8d: the collective energy and drive behind safety initiatives is maintained for the sake of safety management's operation. Without momentum, management structures exist but lack the force to act. The servant (momentum) points at the master (management).

A lagging-indicator IS a specific kind of indicator — a retrospective measurement that signals past performance. All lagging indicators are indicators; the qualified term specifies temporal direction (backward-looking). Nearest kind: indicator.

A lagging-indicator serves the dashboard: the dashboard is built to display retrospective performance data, and lagging-indicators provide exactly that — historical metrics that inform decisions. Law 8d — the indicator is the servant, the dashboard is the master.

Safety-momentum DERIVED_FROM motivation: motivation as a concept (drive, incentive, purpose) existed first and fed into the more specific construct of safety-momentum (collective energy behind safety initiatives). Which existed first? Motivation predates and generically feeds into the safety-specific variant.

A safety-kpi IS a specific kind of kpi — a quantifiable safety performance measure. The general concept of kpi (key performance indicator) is the nearest kind; a competent speaker calls a safety-kpi 'a kpi'. Law 9.
A safety-reward IS a specific kind of incentive — one structured to reinforce safety behaviors. A competent speaker calls a safety reward 'a type of incentive'. Nearest kind is incentive (Law 9).

Safety-reward is designed and maintained for the sake of safety-management. Rewards are a tool safety managers use to reinforce desired safety behaviors and culture — the purpose is teleological (Law 8d), not a removal dependency.

A near-miss is a specific kind of safety-incident: it is an unplanned event in a safety context that had the potential to cause harm but did not, due to chance or timely intervention. Nearest kind is safety-incident (Law 9). Which-came-first: safety-incident (epoch 0, more foundational) predates near-miss (epoch 0.15), consistent with INSTANCE_OF direction.

A hazard-register SERVES hazard-assessment (Law 8d): the register is built and maintained for the sake of hazard-assessment's operation. It catalogs hazards systematically to support the assessment process — its designed purpose is to further hazard-assessment. For whose sake? The servant (hazard-register) points at the master (hazard-assessment).

Safety-KPIs are maintained for the sake of safety-guidelines (Law 8d): they measure compliance with and effectiveness of guidelines, making guidelines operational and trackable. The KPIs serve the guidelines — servant points at master.

safety-audit is maintained for the sake of safety-guidelines: audits exist to verify compliance with, and effectiveness of, guidelines. The designed purpose of an audit is to serve the guideline — the servant points at the master.

safety-baseline IS a specific kind of safety-management approach — it establishes baseline safety standards and metrics that management uses as reference points. 'A safety baseline' is commonly called 'a management baseline' in safety practice.
A safety-signature IS a specific kind of pattern-recognition construct — it detects subtle, recurring behavioral and operational cues that signal underlying safety culture health or decay.
Safety-signature is maintained for the sake of safety-analysis: it provides the early-warning cues that analysis interprets into actionable insight. Servant (signature) points at master (analysis).

Safety-signals are maintained for the sake of safety-management: they are visible cues placed in the work environment to keep safety top-of-mind and signal organizational commitment to management. The servant (signals) points at the master (management).

A safety-snapshot is a point-in-time record maintained for the sake of safety-analysis: it provides the raw observational data that analysis transforms into insight. The servant (snapshot) points at the master (analysis).

A safety-reminder exists for the sake of safety-management: reminders sustain management practices by keeping protocols and priorities salient for workers and managers alike. Servant (reminder) points at master (management).

Safety-signals IS a specific kind of safety-indicator: they are visible cues placed in the work environment that indicate safety priorities and organizational commitment. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls a safety signal a type of indicator — it signals/indicates the state of safety culture.

A safety-snapshot IS a specific kind of safety-metric: it is a point-in-time measurement of safety conditions, performance, or culture. Like any metric, it quantifies a specific dimension; unlike a trend, it captures a single moment. The note 'point-in-time record' confirms it is a metric by definition.

A safety-benchmark is a specific kind of safety-metric: it is a measured reference point used to evaluate safety performance. Like any metric, it quantifies a dimension of safety; the benchmark is the specific value or range that serves as the reference standard. A competent speaker calls a safety benchmark a type of safety metric.
A safety-benchmark IS a specific kind of safety-indicator: it signals a reference value against which performance is judged. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls a benchmark a kind of indicator.
A safety-snapshot IS a specific kind of safety-indicator: it signals the current state of safety conditions at a point in time. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls a snapshot a kind of indicator.

A safety-symptom IS a specific kind of safety-indicator: it is a visible or measurable sign (near-miss, early warning signal) that indicates underlying safety conditions or trends. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call a symptom a kind of indicator — it signals something about the state of safety.

A safety-snapshot SERVES safety-reporting: the point-in-time data captured by a snapshot provides the observational basis that reporting transforms into structured accounts of safety conditions. The servant (snapshot) points at the master (reporting) — snapshots are created for the sake of reporting.

A safety-baseline IS a specific kind of safety-indicator: it establishes a reference value against which safety performance is measured and signals whether current conditions meet the expected standard. Per Law 9, a competent speaker calls a baseline a kind of indicator.

A safety-benchmark SERVES safety-management: benchmarks are reference values set to evaluate safety performance, and they are maintained for the sake of management's ability to assess and steer safety outcomes. The benchmark serves management — the master — by providing the standards against which progress is judged.

A safety-baseline SERVES safety-management: a baseline is a reference point established to measure progress and evaluate performance, maintained for the sake of management's oversight function. It provides the starting reference that management needs to track improvements.

A safety-snapshot SERVES safety-management: point-in-time captures of safety conditions exist for the sake of management's situational awareness and decision-making. Management uses snapshots to understand current state.

A safety-trainer IS a specific kind of safety-management: it is a tool or instrument used by management to build and sustain safety competence across the organization. Per Law 9, it is a management mechanism for safety. Files against nearest kind.

A safety-audit is a specific kind of safety-procedure: it follows a defined process to examine compliance and effectiveness. The removal test: remove safety-procedure and safety-audit cannot operate — audits require procedural structure.

Tested: safety-assessment IS a specific kind of safety-evaluation — per Law 9. Safety-assessment applies evaluation methods to a particular context, making it a subtype of the general safety-evaluation construct.

A safety-debrief is organized for the sake of safety-learning: its designed purpose is to extract lessons from incidents and events, turning experience into organizational knowledge. Per Law 8d, the servant (debrief) points at the master (learning).

A safety-debrief IS a specific kind of safety-review — both are structured processes for examining past events, but a debrief is specifically oriented toward learning extraction rather than compliance or certification. Per Law 9.

The safety-tracker is built and maintained for the sake of safety-evaluation: it collects and organizes the raw data (incidents, metrics, observations) that evaluations require to function. Remove the tracker and evaluations lose their data source — the purpose is by design.

The hierarchy of controls is a designed framework for selecting and implementing safety measures. Its purpose is to serve safety-management by providing the structured decision logic that managers use to control risk. It exists for the sake of safety management, not because management needs it to operate at all.

Safety-evaluation is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it produces the structured assessments that managers need to make decisions about resource allocation, risk treatment, and program direction. Remove evaluation and management loses its evidence base — it is designed to serve management's decision cycle.

A safety-stop is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: it provides the procedural authority and mechanism for halting operations when safety is at risk, serving as a critical intervention tool within the safety management system.

A safety-walk is a specific kind of safety-observation: it is the practice of systematically observing work areas for hazards, making it a structured instance of the broader safety-observation concept.

A safety-hierarchy-of-controls is a specific kind of risk-control: it is the systematic ranking of control measures (elimination → substitution → engineering → administrative → PPE) by effectiveness, making it a structured instance of risk-control.

A safety-audit is a specific kind of safety-evaluation: it is a systematic, independent examination of safety systems and performance, making it a structured instance of the broader safety-evaluation concept.

A safety-snapshot is a specific kind of safety-management instrument: a point-in-time record of safety conditions, performance data, and compliance status that enables managers to assess and direct safety operations.

safety-documentation is a specific kind of documentation: the practice of recording, organizing, and maintaining safety-related information. A competent speaker would call it 'a kind of documentation'.

risk-appetite is designed for the sake of risk-management: it sets the boundaries within which risk decisions are made, serving the purpose of calibrating how much risk the organization is willing to accept.
safety-capacity is literally a part of safety-management: the organized capability (trained personnel, tools, equipment) that safety-management contains and deploys to prevent and respond to events.
Safety moments are brief safety talks used to enact and communicate organizational safety commitments — the practice serves the purpose of making the commitment operational and visible.

A safety-snapshot is a specific kind of safety-documentation: it is a recorded observation of conditions, preserving knowledge about hazards — fitting squarely under documentation's practice of recording information.

A safety-reminder is a specific kind of safety-documentation: a brief, recorded prompt that preserves safety-relevant information for later recall. A competent speaker would call it 'a kind of safety-documentation'. The test: which came first? documentation preceded reminders; but INSTANCE_OF is kind-of, not historical. Safety-documentation records information; safety-reminders are brief records designed to prompt recall.

Safety-documentation is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: its designed purpose is to further management's operation by recording, communicating, and preserving safety-relevant information. Per Law 8d, the teleological arrow points servant→master — documentation serves management, not the reverse.

Safety-capacity — the organizational capability to execute safety work — is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management. Per Law 8d, the teleological arrow points servant→master: capacity serves management. Removing capacity would impair management's operation, but this edge files the purpose relation (SERVES), not the dependency relation.

Safety-prevention is built and maintained for the sake of safety-management: its purpose is to implement proactive measures that prevent harm before it occurs, serving management's objective of reducing risk. Per Law 8d, the teleological arrow points servant→master.

A safety-audit is a specific kind of safety-review: a systematic, independent examination of whether safety activities and results comply with planned arrangements and are properly implemented. A competent speaker would call an audit a type of review. Per Law 9, this is specific→general.

A safety-review is a specific kind of safety-evaluation: a structured assessment of safety performance, controls, and outcomes. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call a review a type of evaluation — the review is the narrower, more specific practice within the broader evaluation category.

Safety-prevention is built and maintained for the sake of risk-management: its designed purpose is to reduce risk through proactive measures, which is risk-management's core operation. Per Law 8d: for-whose-sake test — safety-prevention serves as the servant to risk-management's master objective. Removing risk-management as a domain does not stop safety-prevention from operating; rather, safety-prevention exists to further risk-management's aims.

A safety-prevention is a specific kind of safety-control (Law 9). Prevention measures — engineering controls, administrative procedures, PPE — are all safety controls designed to eliminate or reduce hazard exposure. A competent speaker would call a prevention measure a type of control.

The concept of near-miss derives from hazard (Law 7: which-came-first). Hazard as a concept predates and feeds into near-miss — a near-miss is a hazard instance where the chain of events was interrupted before harm materialized. The DERIVED_FROM direction is hazard → near-miss, which is correct.

safety-training IS a specific kind of safety-evaluation. Training programs evaluate and develop competence — they assess knowledge gaps, evaluate learning outcomes, and evaluate performance improvement.

Safety-training is designed and maintained for the sake of building safety-competence (Law 8d: teleology). The entire purpose of safety training programs is to develop the knowledge, skills, abilities, and attitudes that constitute competence. Remove training as an institution and competence-building loses its primary structured mechanism — organizations still value competence, but their main designed instrument for creating it disappears. The servant (training) points at the master (competence).

safety-training IS a specific kind of safety-education. Education covers the full spectrum from theory to practice; training narrows to hands-on skill development. A competent speaker would call safety-training a form of safety-education. Per Law 9, specific→general.

safety-interval SERVES safety-management per Law 8d. The interval is designed and maintained for the sake of enabling systematic safety oversight — it provides the cadence that management uses to ensure periodic verification. Direction: servant (interval) points at master (management). This is not a dependency (the interval can exist without management executing it) but a teleological relation.

safety-signal INSTANCE_OF safety-indicator (Law 9). A safety-signal is a specific kind of safety-indicator. Indicator is the broader category (any construct that conveys status information); signal is the narrower (an indicator designed to actively communicate a message — e.g. warning light, alarm tone). Specific→general. Nearest kind confirmed by precheck.

Safety-bias IS a specific kind of cognitive-bias. It is a systematic deviation from judgment/safety standards caused by psychological factors, making it a subtype of cognitive bias specific to safety domains. Law 9 test: a competent speaker would call safety-bias a kind of cognitive bias.

Safety-culture-assessment IS a specific kind of safety-evaluation. It assesses and evaluates the state of organizational safety culture — making it a subtype of evaluation focused on culture. Law 9 passes: a competent speaker calls this a kind of safety evaluation.

safety-hierarchy-of-controls is a framework whose purpose is to systematically prevent harm by ranking control measures. It needs the concept of prevention to operate — without prevention as a goal, the hierarchy's ordering (most to least effective) has no meaning. The hierarchy is designed to make prevention systematic and evidence-based.

safety-auditing IS a specific kind of audit — a systematic examination focused on safety-specific activities, procedures, and standards. The nearest kind is 'audit'. Law 9 test: a competent speaker would call safety-auditing 'an audit'.

safety-auditing is built for the sake of evaluation — its purpose is to produce findings that feed into organizational evaluation and decision-making. Law 8d: servant (safety-auditing) → master (evaluation). Remove safety-auditing and evaluation still operates; safety-auditing's designed purpose is to further evaluation.
